correctness.rationale: Exact source-coefficient substitution gives B,C. Symbolic polynomial expansion verifies all three positive/discriminant identities. Case analysis for kappa<=1/2 and kappa>1/2 proves both directions for every n and positive z, including equality and B=C=0. Complex nonreal roots necessarily change sign along integer orbit; when B<0,C<0, a nonzero negative coefficient on the larger-modulus negative root forces eventual negative even iterates. The sharp maximum follows by monotonicity of the two explicit branches. Fraction checker exercises identities independently of floating-point code.

value.rationale: The recent family trades error constants against infinitely stiff damping, yet A-stability does not certify nonnegative intermediate states. A global sharp scalar positivity radius is a natural independent numerical design criterion. The two structural transition mechanisms meet at the unique kappa=1/2 maximizer with radius 3/2, three times the BDF2 endpoint radius. The exact parameter choice and complete global sign classification are substantive beyond a routine coefficient check; they identify a useful accuracy/stiffness/positivity tradeoff without extrapolating to matrices.
